question.leadin: Answer the following questions about famous British explorers who died or disappeared while on their voyages.
question.text: This navigator searched for a Northwest Passage to Asia while sailing the ship Half-Moon on behalf of the Dutch East India Company. This explorer mysteriously disappeared after a 1611 mutiny aboard his ship.
question.clue: This explorer, who employed the navigator Abacuk Pricket, sailed on the Half Moon to search for the Northwest Passage on behalf of the Dutch East India Company.

swap.text: The Normans were led at Hastings by this man, who became King of England afterwards and commissioned the Domesday Book.
swap.answerHtml: William the Conqueror [or William I; or William the Bastard; or William II of Normandy; accept Guillaume in place of William; prompt on William]
swap.clue: This ruler died after the Siege of Mantes, where he fell off a horse.

question.leadin: This woman's ascension rights were restored with the Third Succession Act of 1543, though she and her younger sister remained legally illegitimate.
question.text: Name this Catholic queen of England who deposed Lady Jane Grey to become queen after the death of her younger half-brother, Edward VI.
question.clue: Wyatt's Rebellion occurred in protest of this monarch's marriage to Philip II of Spain, during which she experienced several phantom pregnancies.

swap.leadin: Name these Prime Ministers who belonged to the Labour Party of the United Kingdom.
swap.text: This man became the first Labour Party Prime Minister in 1924, but was later kicked out due to his creation of the National Government.
swap.clue: Oswald Mosley served as this man's Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, but later resigned to found the New Party.

question.leadin: She was also known as Alexandrina.
question.text: Name this monarch whose reign was the longest in British history until Elizabeth II's overtook it in 2015.
question.clue: This monarch kept Lord Melbourne as prime minister during the "bedchamber crisis" and refused the demands of Sir Robert Peel.

swap.leadin: He served as Chancellor of the Exchequer in the short-lived Who? Who? Ministry.
swap.text: Name this Jewish leader of the Protectionist wing of the Conservative party known for his feud with William Gladstone.
swap.clue: He drafted legislation giving the vote to every adult male houseowner living in a borough, the Second Reform Act.

question.leadin: Answer the following about early radicals in British history.
question.text: During this king's reign, the Middlesex By-Election Controversy occurred over whether to seat the radical John Wilkes. This king is more notable for having lost the American Revolutionary War.
question.clue: During this ruler's reign, John Wilkes led troops against men who had destroyed Newgate Prison to protest the Papists Act.

swap.leadin: At a crucial point in this battle, Sir William Stanley decided to support the eventual winner.
swap.text: Name this battle fought near Ambion Hill. The Earl of Northumberland's failure to lead his troops into this battle contributed to its outcome.
swap.clue: The leader of the losing army managed to unhorse John Cheyne and kill Sir William Brandon, but failed to receive assistance from Henry Percy's reserves.

question.text: This member of the earlier Hohenstaufen family succeeded Frederick Barbarossa and gained control of Sicily by marrying Constance I. An English king of this name and number founded Eton College and faced Jack Cade's Revolt.
question.clue: This king was deposed and fled to Scotland following the Battle of Towton.

swap.text: In England, old tally sticks were regularly destroyed by the holder of this office. The holder of this office traditionally brings a red Despatch Box to Parliament to read a speech on a Wednesday in March.
swap.answerHtml: Chancellor of the Exchequer [prompt on chancellor; prompt on Second Lord of the Treasury] (the day being referred to is Budget Day)
swap.clue: Both Walpole and Churchill also held this economic position during their careers, which sets the inflationary target for British banks and spending limits for ministerial departments.

question.leadin: Answer the following about John Bull, the national personification of Great Britain.
question.text: An actual person named John Bull is a composer sometimes credited with writing this British national anthem, whose title changes depending on if the monarch is male or female.
question.answerHtml: "God Save the King" [or "God Save the Queen"]

swap.leadin: This politician intervened in the Ford machinists' strike of 1968 and published the white paper In Place of Strife while serving as Employment Secretary in 1969.
swap.text: Name this MP for Blackburn who served as both Secretary of State for Health and Minister for Transport in the 1960s and 1970s. This woman was frozen out when her rival James Callaghan became Prime Minister.
swap.clue: Following a protracted series of on-and-off strikes throughout the 1960s, this Secretary of State for Employment and Productivity proposed a White Paper called In Place of Strife in 1969, which imposed requirements that had to be met before a strike was called.

question.leadin: This man's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum is a massive treatise of alchemy compiled from various famous authors.
question.text: Name this English collector, numismatist, and Freemason. He donated his cabinet of curiosities, much of which was obtained from the Tradescants of Lambeth, to his namesake museum.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about British scandals of 1963.
swap.text: Conservative Prime Minister Harold Macmillan resigned in 1963 amid the fallout from an "affair" when this Secretary of State for War lied about his extramarital relations with 19-year-old model Christine Keeler.
swap.clue: In 1960, this man was appointed to the position of Secretary of State for War by Harold Macmillan.

question.leadin: Answer some questions on the economic history of the counties of Kent, Sussex, and Dorset.
question.text: The Mermaid and Olde Bell inns in this town were connected by a secret passage and used by the Hawkhurst Gang. This town replaced New Romney as one of the Cinque Ports after the River Rother changed course.

swap.leadin: Name these practitioners of the fabled "honorable resignation" in post-war British politics.
swap.text: This sometime Labour Foreign Secretary resigned from Tony Blair's Cabinet in 2003 in protest over the invasion of Iraq.

question.text: This Labour Home Secretary oversaw the passage of the Sexual Offences Act in 1967, which partially decriminalized homosexuality, in addition to laws legalizing abortion and banning capital punishment.
question.answerHtml: Roy Jenkins [or Roy Harris Jenkins, Baron Jenkins of Hillhead]
question.clue: This man who became MP for Glasgow-Hillhead in a significant 1982 victory, and had presided over the legalization of abortion, abolition of capital punishment, and relaxation of divorce law during his tenure as Home Secretary from 1965-67.

swap.text: On the recapture of South Georgia, Margaret Thatcher jingoistically told reporters to "congratulate our armed forces and the Marines" and to do this action. Ted Heath is said to have sardonically repeated this word after Thatcher resigned.
swap.answerHtml: “rejoice” [or word forms such as rejoicing; accept “just rejoice at that news and congratulate our forces and the Marines”; accept “rejoice, rejoice”; accept “rejoice, rejoice, rejoice”]

question.text: Use of the "V" sign among resistance groups was encouraged by this British organization, whose members were nicknamed the "Baker Street Irregulars" and primarily carried out sabotage operations.
question.clue: This British organisation aided the French resistance in Operation Jedburgh and were sometimes nicknamed 'the Baker Street Irregulars' or 'Churchill's Secret Army'.

swap.leadin: This product of the Committee on Social and Allied Services suggested that want, disease, ignorance, squalor, and idleness were the five "Giant Evils."
swap.text: Identify this 1942 document, which instigated the foundation of the National Health Service and other components of the British welfare state. It was named for the chairman of the committee that produced it.
swap.clue: This document identified squalor, ignorance, want, idleness, and disease as the "Five Giant Evils" plaguing society.
